For a small brand, direct China-to-customer shipping under Section 321 can be a useful test channel, but it is a fragile foundation for the whole supply chain.

The apparent advantage is meaningful: a qualifying shipment valued at $800 or less can enter without ordinary customs duties and taxes, allowing an overseas seller to avoid the import-duty cost of bulk inventory and price more aggressively. [shard_04647_72515] [shard_01754_13790]

That saving is not the same as “free shipping,” because your real comparison is landed unit cost: product cost, packaging, international postage, fuel and handling surcharges, customs-clearance charges, payment and platform fees, returns, replacements, customer service, and inventory carrying cost. [shard_02137_49188] [shard_01332_28146]

Air freight is especially easy to underestimate because carriers may charge on volumetric weight rather than actual weight, then add fuel, handling, and clearance charges. [shard_01332_28146]

Indicative China-US air delivery can be roughly seven to ten days in one shipping model, while other air-freight services quote about six to thirteen days or one to four days for express service, so the supplier’s promised transit time should be tested against the service level actually purchased. [shard_04003_29557] [shard_05461_22280]

Those times also exclude the variability created by customs holds, incomplete invoices, bad HS classifications, inaccurate descriptions, and peak-season carrier congestion. [shard_05461_22280]

Every parcel still needs accurate commercial information, including the manufacturer’s country of origin, shipper and recipient details, HS code, and a truthful description rather than a “gift” designation. [shard_05461_22280]

Do not accept a supplier’s promise to use “tax-inclusive” or “tax-free” shipping as a substitute for understanding who is importing, who is paying duty if the shipment is challenged, and whether the declaration is accurate, because DDU and DDP arrangements allocate customs work and charges differently. [shard_01130_48980] [shard_04003_29557]

I could not establish from the available material whether the $800 China-to-US treatment is still unchanged on 23 July 2026, so obtain a current written ruling or broker assessment for each product and do not build your pricing around the assumption that the exemption is permanent. [shard_02612_34845]

The policy risk is asymmetric: if enforcement tightens, the direct-ship model can lose its duty advantage across thousands of customer parcels at once, whereas inventory already imported into the US has a more predictable landed cost even though it paid applicable duties upfront. [shard_03415_76201] [shard_02612_34845]
